title: Hantavirus and oral health care preparedness
html: The attention to hantavirus infections has renewed concerns about preparedness for emerging zoonotic diseases, highlighting both the unpredictable nature of zoonotic pathogens and the continued vulnerability of global health systems to infectious threats.1 Although the overall public health risk remains relatively low in most settings, the reemergence of hantavirus highlights a broader question for oral health care systems: Have the lessons learned during the COVID-19 pandemic been adequately translated into sustainable preparedness strategies for future infectious threats?
